span.note: status: the paper's own words: remains to be determined · differs in: THE AXIS IS WIDESPREAD AGAINST NECESSARY. 'Quotation withheld As was shown in a previous study ..., IT IS LIKELY THAT ONLY A SUBSET OF BRAIN REGIONS ARE NECESSARY FOR TASK PERFORMANCE.' The paper's own headline observation is separated from the inference a reader would draw from it, BY THE PAPER, before anyone else can draw it. Extent is measured; necessity is not, and the two are different experiments. Q-501.

span.label: More than half of the ~24,000 neurons recorded across 34 brain regions changed their firing with the thirst task, responding rapidly to the water-predicting odour cue before sustained water-acquisition activity.
span.note: retracted: RE-GROUNDED - THE POINTER WAS WRONG, NOT THE CLAIM. The old evidence was verbatim, anchored and correctly cut, and it contained NONE of this claim's numbers (000, 24, 34). The paper states the claim in one sentence elsewhere and the tagger did not use it. CLAUDE_B, 2026-08-23: `WE HAVE SPENT THE DAY VERIFYING THAT QUOTES ARE REAL AND NONE OF IT ASKS WHETHER THEY ARE RELEVANT.` Confirmed by reading the claim, the old span and the candidate together; the candidate carries every number AND the claim's own content words.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The rewarded odour cue triggered a wave of activity that started in olfactory regions about 150 ms after odour onset and reached every recorded brain region within about 300 ms.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Satiety gated the wave: once mice were sated the identical odour cue produced only a brief transient change in firing and no licking.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Spontaneous pre-stimulus baseline firing, not just cue-evoked firing, shifted with satiety state in neurons across many brain regions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Odour identity could be decoded from populations throughout the brain in thirsty mice, but decoding fell to near chance across much of the brain once the mice were sated.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Single neurons were specialised: each mostly encoded one task aspect (state, cue, or behaviour), while every brain region held a mixture of all these neuron types.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Optogenetic stimulation of hypothalamic thirst neurons in sated mice pushed behaviour, within-trial brainwide dynamics, and single-neuron satiety correlates back to their thirsty-state values.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Re-creating the thirst representation in only a subset of brain regions was enough to restore thirst-motivated sensory processing, behaviour and the associated brainwide dynamics.

span.label: the Go cue produced a wave of activity that began in olfactory regions within about 150 ms and reached every recorded region within about 300 ms
